styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small single-tile fence section. It shows a wooden post and corrugated sheets with a top-edge ridge and a short front face. It carries 17 visible tones per 16x16 tile, level with the stall (17) and the well (20) and well above the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans brown/rust toward the neighbouring material instead of being a black sticker line. The metal ramp reads as about 4 steps (highlight, light, mid, dark) with rust and grain speckle, one step short of the references' 5-6. The scrap-metal texture is varied and the post is shaded separately from the sheets. The piece is as dense as the references and does not look thinner or flatter beside them. A slightly shallower ramp is not enough to fail it.

answer.evidence: The sheet has a 1-row dark outline at row 3, then a light row 4 and a mid-tone row 5 in blue-grey. Row 6 is slightly darker, with no clear front-edge line. The post (rows 0-15) is drawn as a vertical strip with only a thin tan cap at rows 0-1. The whole piece reads as a flat front elevation with at most a rim at the top.
